summary:
West Sumatra stands under Indonesia's national legal framework, which carries the criminal provisions, document rules and entry regime; what follows is specific to the province.

Two local instruments in West Sumatra restrict LGBT people. Bukittinggi City's Regional Regulation No. 2 of 2024 on Public Order targets LGBT people and is framed as an expression of local religious values and Minangkabau customary norms. In Limapuluh Kota regency the regional legislature finalised a draft anti-LGBT regulation on 13 May 2026, folded into a Public Order and Tranquillity (Trantibum) regulation; the chair of the drafting body said the drafting stages had reached finalisation.

The Limapuluh Kota text provides for administrative fines and rehabilitation for LGBT people. Neither instrument is recorded as carrying criminal penalties; the sanctions documented are administrative fines and mandated rehabilitation, which directs LGBT people into a corrective programme rather than a fine alone.

Both instruments operate through public-order powers rather than the criminal code, so their reach is conduct in public space in the two named localities. No West Sumatra-specific enforcement action, arrest or prosecution appears in the source inventory, so a trans visitor's exposure in the province rests on these two instruments and on the national framework.
tangentialFactors:
A 2022 survey by OutRight Action International mapped discriminatory regional regulations across eight Indonesian provinces, among them Aceh, DKI Jakarta, East Kalimantan, Lampung, North Sumatra, South Sulawesi, South Sumatra and Yogyakarta. West Sumatra was not among them, and the Bukittinggi regulation postdates that survey, so the province has moved into the group of jurisdictions using the regional-bylaw route since the mapping was published.

Indonesian academic commentary treats the Bukittinggi regulation as an implementation of Islamic governance principles, which indicates the instrument's religious and customary basis is not contested in local scholarship.
localsOnly:
Residents of Bukittinggi live under a city public-order regulation that targets LGBT people, and residents of Limapuluh Kota regency face a finalised draft regulation carrying administrative fines and rehabilitation for LGBT people.

The Limapuluh Kota instrument was drafted by the regency legislature, which is the body that finalised it in May 2026. The inventory records no equivalent instrument in other West Sumatran regencies, so the regency-level drafting process is documented in one regency and one city only.
outOfScopeNotes:
No West Sumatra enforcement record, arrest, prosecution or violence incident is sourced. Whether Bukittinggi's Regional Regulation No. 2 of 2024 is being enforced, and against whom, is not documented.

The Limapuluh Kota regulation was finalised at drafting stage as of 13 May 2026; its promulgation status, effective date and the schedule of administrative fines are not sourced, and the content of the rehabilitation requirement is not described in the inventory.

No West Sumatra-specific rules on identity documents, facilities, screening or healthcare access were identified. The 2022 OutRight mapping predates both instruments and therefore does not describe current West Sumatran coverage.
